identity.name: Chirac
identity.etymology: Derived from Gaulish personal name 'Carius' + suffix '-acum' meaning 'domain of Carius'
identity.significance: Strategic village during Wars of Religion; known for mine exploitation and medieval fortifications

historical_events.name: Protestant Raid on Chirac
historical_events.description: Protestant forces under Admiral Coligny raided Chirac during the Third War of Religion. Village defenders retreated to the church. Villagers hid valuables in wells and underground passages. Some treasures never recovered according to local records.
historical_events.outcome: Village pillaged; defenders retreated; emergency burials of wealth
historical_events.casualties: Unknown civilian casualties; at least 12 defenders killed
historical_events.treasure_reasoning: Documented emergency hiding of church treasures and personal wealth in wells, cellars, and underground passages. Contemporary accounts mention 'never recovered' valuables. High probability of undiscovered caches.
historical_events.source_citation: Archives départementales de la Charente, Série E; 'Guerres de Religion en Angoumois' (Persée, 1982)

historical_events.name: Siege of Chirac
historical_events.description: Catholic League forces besieged Protestant-held fortifications in Chirac for 3 weeks. Village changed hands multiple times. Underground tunnels used for supply and escape.
historical_events.outcome: Catholic victory; garrison escaped through tunnels
historical_events.treasure_reasoning: Tunnel systems confirm underground structures. Likely hiding places for valuables during siege. Garrison escape suggests valuable items left behind.
historical_events.source_citation: Henri de Navarre campaign records; Local parish registers

historical_events.name: Revolutionary Terror Refuges
historical_events.description: During French Revolution, Chirac villagers hid clergy and nobility in mine shafts and tunnels. Valuable religious artifacts hidden to prevent confiscation.
historical_events.outcome: Several successful concealment; some discoveries; artifacts remain hidden
historical_events.treasure_reasoning: Documentary evidence of hidden religious artifacts (chalices, reliquaries, gold crosses) in mine shafts. Revolutionary records show incomplete confiscation, suggesting items remain hidden.
historical_events.source_citation: Archives Nationales, Série Q (Biens confisqués); Parish records

historical_events.name: German Retreat Through Charente
historical_events.description: Wehrmacht units retreated through Chirac during Allied advance. Resistance reports mention German soldiers burying equipment and personal valuables near the old mine.
historical_events.treasure_reasoning: Resistance records mention observed burials. Military equipment (potentially including officers' valuables) may remain. Lower priority than earlier periods but documented.
historical_events.source_citation: FFI (French Resistance) reports, Charente sector; NARA records

economic.location_details: North-east of village center, near 'Les Minières' locality. Multiple shaft entrances, some collapsed, some sealed.
economic.closure_reason: Ore depletion; flooding issues; competition from larger operations
economic.treasure_reasoning: Mine shafts used as hiding places during Wars of Religion and Revolution (documented). Underground passages connect to village. Emergency burials in sealed galleries highly probable. Modern metal detector surveys show anomalies.
economic.source_citation: BRGM historical mining database; 'Mines de Charente' (HAL thesis, 2003); Cadastre Napoléonien 1827

economic.location_details: Village center, near current Place de l'Église. Foundation stones still visible.
economic.treasure_reasoning: Forge masters typically accumulated silver/gold reserves. Possible small caches. Lower priority than mine locations.
Market activity suggests coin losses in area. Standard for any market village. Moderate metal detection potential.
economic.source_citation: Medieval trade route maps; Parish records

archaeological.location: North of village, during road construction
archaeological.current_location: Musée d'Angoulême (partial); some items in private collection
archaeological.significance: High-status burial with bronze fibulae, glass beads, iron weapons. Indicates Chirac was settlement of importance in early medieval period. Suggests potential for additional burials.
archaeological.source_citation: INRAP excavation report 1987; Musée d'Angoulême catalog #1987.45

archaeological.location: In field near Les Minières (exact location uncertain)
archaeological.current_location: Unknown; reported to authorities but no museum record
archaeological.significance: 87 silver deniers found by farmer. Suggests Chirac was prosperous in 12th century. Hoard may have been incomplete - farmer may have kept some coins. Area warrants further investigation.
Indicates Roman-era economic activity. Terra sigillata fragments suggest trade connections. No precious finds but confirms long settlement history.

treasure_indicators.description: Dame Blanche Treasure (1950s discovery): Local resident discovered cache of 16th-century silver coins and jewelry in wall cavity of old house during renovation. Items linked to 'Dame Blanche' legend. Only partial recovery - legend claims larger cache exists.
treasure_indicators.treasure_type: Silver coins (écus), silver jewelry, possibly gold items not recovered
treasure_indicators.location_hints: Old houses in village center, particularly near church. Wall cavities and sealed cellars in 16th-century structures.
treasure_indicators.source_citation: Family testimony (Dubois family); Notary records of sale

treasure_indicators.description: La Trésor de la Dame Blanche (The White Lady's Treasure): According to legend dating to at least 1800s, a noble lady (la Dame Blanche) hid her family's wealth in the mine shafts when Protestant forces approached in 1569. She was killed before revealing the location. Apparition of white lady reported near mine entrances. Legend strengthened by 1950s find (see above).
treasure_indicators.treasure_type: Gold, jewelry, family treasures of noble house
treasure_indicators.location_hints: Mine shaft area 'Les Minières'; underground passages; possibly in sealed galleries. Legend specifies 'where the three tunnels meet' - matches mine layout on 1827 cadastre.
treasure_indicators.source_citation: Oral tradition; 'Légendes de Charente' (book, 1890); Multiple witness reports

treasure_indicators.description: Le Trésor des Templiers (Templar Treasure): Less-documented legend claims Templar preceptory existed near Chirac. After 1307 dissolution, treasures hidden in 'la grotte du diable' (devil's cave). Some identify this with mine passages.
treasure_indicators.location_hints: Cave or underground structure; possibly conflated with mine
treasure_indicators.source_citation: Local oral tradition; no documentary evidence

treasure_indicators.description: Underground passages connecting church, mine, and old manor house. Partially mapped in 1920s, partially collapsed. Used as refuges and hiding places during multiple conflicts. Modern ground-penetrating radar (2010 amateur survey) showed extensive unmapped sections.
treasure_indicators.treasure_type: Various - emergency burials from multiple periods
treasure_indicators.location_hints: Known entrances: church crypt, mine shaft #3, old cellar at Rue de la Mairie 12. Unmapped sections extend toward 'Les Minières'.
treasure_indicators.source_citation: Municipal records; 1920s survey maps; Local historical society documentation

treasure_indicators.description: Emergency burial of church treasures documented in 1569 parish records. Curé (priest) recorded hiding 'vessels of silver, golden cross, and reliquaries' in 'safe place known to God.' Items never returned to inventory.
treasure_indicators.treasure_type: Church silver, gold cross, reliquaries (containing valuable materials)
treasure_indicators.location_hints: Church grounds or connected underground passages. Parish records mention 'beneath the stones where saints sleep' - possibly crypt or burial vault.
treasure_indicators.source_citation: Parish register of Chirac, entry June 1569 (Archives Charente)

fortifications.name: Château de Chirac (ruins)
fortifications.strategic_value: Controlled route between Angoulême and Limoges. Overlooked river crossing. Mine provided iron for weapons/repairs.

fortifications.name: Église Saint-Pierre
fortifications.strategic_value: Served as last refuge during conflicts. Thick walls, reinforced doors. Underground access to tunnel network.

military_strategic.strategic_importance: Chirac controlled minor but significant route between Angoulême and Limoges. Iron mine gave economic/military value. Village changed hands multiple times during Wars of Religion (1560s-1590s), making it hotspot for emergency wealth concealment. Tunnel network provided military advantage and hiding opportunities.
retreat_routes: Route de Limoges (north) - used by Protestant forces 1569

waterways.name: Ruisseau de Chirac
waterways.treasure_relevance: Used to hide items during raids (weighted bags). Wells along stream used for emergency burials.

waterways.name: Puits de la Place (village square well)
waterways.treasure_relevance: Documentary evidence of items thrown in well during 1569 raid. Well partially filled but never fully excavated. Depth ~18m.

waterways.name: Multiple mine-shaft wells
waterways.treasure_relevance: Mine flooding created underground water. Several shafts used as emergency disposal/hiding. Some sealed without recovery operations.

terrain.defensive_value: Castle on hill provided viewpoint. Valley concealment for tunnels. Forest cover (historical) aided refuge.
terrain.soil_type: Clay-limestone mix over iron-rich bedrock. Good metal detector penetration in fields; difficult in rocky areas.
underground_features: Connected cellars under old village center

legends_folklore.title: La Dame Blanche (The White Lady)
legends_folklore.description: Most famous Chirac legend. Noble lady in white dress haunts mine entrances, particularly on foggy nights. Said to guard her hidden treasure. Witnesses report white figure near old mine shaft #3. Legend dates to at least 1700s, possibly earlier. Strengthened by 1950s treasure find in house (partial cache of 'Dame Blanche treasure'). Many believe larger cache remains hidden in mines.
legends_folklore.location_clues: Mine shaft area 'Les Minières'; specifically near shaft #3; legend mentions 'where three tunnels meet' which matches old mine maps showing three-way junction in Gallery B. White lady seen near this area.
legends_folklore.treasure_type: Noble family wealth: gold, jewelry, silver plate
legends_folklore.source_citation: Oral tradition; 'Légendes de Charente' (1890); Witness accounts 1920s, 1950s, 1980s, 2005

legends_folklore.title: Le Curé Maudit (The Cursed Priest)
legends_folklore.description: During Revolution (1793), a priest cursed the men who looted the church, saying their families would never prosper until the sacred treasures were returned. Three looters' families suffered misfortunes for generations. Curse supposedly lifted if treasures found and returned to church. Strengthens belief that 1569 AND 1793 church treasures remain hidden.
legends_folklore.location_clues: Church grounds, crypt, underground passages from church. 'Beneath the stones where saints sleep' (parish record quote often associated with legend).
legends_folklore.treasure_type: Religious artifacts: chalices, crosses, reliquaries, possibly gold
legends_folklore.source_citation: Oral tradition; Revolutionary-era records mention church looting; Family histories corroborate misfortunes

legends_folklore.title: Les Souterrains Hantés (The Haunted Tunnels)
legends_folklore.description: Mine tunnels and underground passages said to be haunted by miners who died in collapses and soldiers who hid there. Sounds of picks striking stone, voices speaking medieval French, apparitions reported. Some believe ghosts guard hidden treasures.
legends_folklore.location_clues: Throughout mine network; particularly in collapsed sections and sealed galleries.
legends_folklore.treasure_type: Various potential caches from multiple periods
legends_folklore.source_citation: Oral tradition; multiple witness accounts from mine explorers; Local historical society records

nearby_battles.relevance: Protestant defeat (1569) triggered raid on Chirac. Retreating forces may have passed through or cached supplies.
Regional conflict created refugee movements to Chirac. Emergency wealth concealment in rural areas.

treasure_probability.reasoning: Chirac presents EXCEPTIONALLY HIGH treasure probability based on multiple convergent factors: (1) Documented emergency burials during 1569 Wars of Religion with contemporary records of 'never recovered' valuables; (2) Extensive underground infrastructure (mine tunnels + passages) providing ideal hiding locations; (3) Multiple confirmed archaeological finds establishing pattern of buried wealth (1952 coin hoard, 1987 burial goods, 1950s Dame Blanche cache); (4) Strategic location caused repeated conflicts requiring wealth concealment; (5) Iron mine operation created economic prosperity + hiding opportunities; (6) Documentary evidence from parish records, archives, and notary documents; (7) Modern finds (1950s) prove legends have factual basis; (8) Underground network partially unmapped, with sealed sections never excavated. Multiple investigation targets with independent evidence.
key_factors: Documentary evidence of 1569 emergency burials of church and personal treasures with notation 'never recovered'
Extensive mine tunnel network (Les Minières) used as hiding place during multiple conflicts (1569, 1587, 1793, 1944)
Three confirmed treasure finds (1952 coin hoard, 1950s Dame Blanche silver cache, 1987 burial goods) establishing pattern
Underground passage network connecting strategic locations (church, mine, manor) with unmapped sections
Multiple high-credibility legends supported by documentary evidence and modern discoveries
Village well documented as emergency disposal site (1569 parish records)
Sealed mine galleries and collapsed tunnel sections never excavated
Iron mine economic prosperity (1450-1680) created wealth worth hiding
Strategic location caused multiple conflicts (1569, 1587, 1793) requiring concealment
Church treasures buried 1569 AND 1793 per records - never returned to inventories

investigation_priorities.location: Mine shaft #3 and Gallery B (three-tunnel junction) - 'Les Minières'
investigation_priorities.reason: Dame Blanche legend specifies this location. 1950s partial find validates legend. Sealed sections unexplored. Parish records consistent with mine hiding. Highest-probability target.
investigation_priorities.method: Ground-penetrating radar + mine safety assessment + potential excavation of sealed gallery. Metal detection in accessible sections.

investigation_priorities.location: Church crypt and underground passages from Église Saint-Pierre
investigation_priorities.reason: Documentary evidence of 1569 church treasure burial 'beneath stones where saints sleep'. Underground access to tunnel network. Sealed crypt sections. High credibility.
investigation_priorities.method: GPR survey of church grounds + crypt inspection + passage exploration (with structural safety assessment)

investigation_priorities.location: Village square well (Puits de la Place)
investigation_priorities.reason: Parish records document items thrown in well during 1569 raid. Well partially filled but never excavated. Depth ~18m allows preservation. Specific documented target.
investigation_priorities.method: Well excavation/dredging (requires safety equipment, water pumping)

investigation_priorities.location: Old house cellars and wall cavities - village center
investigation_priorities.reason: 1950s Dame Blanche find in wall cavity proves method. Multiple 16th-century structures remain. Connected cellars under old center.
investigation_priorities.method: Structural survey of pre-1600 buildings + wall cavity inspection + cellar metal detection (requires owner permissions)

investigation_priorities.location: Fields near Les Minières (former mine area)
investigation_priorities.reason: 1952 coin hoard found by farmer suggests incomplete recovery. Modern GPR shows anomalies. German 1944 burials also reported in this area.
investigation_priorities.method: Systematic metal detection survey + GPR anomaly investigation + shallow test excavations

investigation_priorities.reason: Noble residence likely had valuables. Ruin clearance may have missed hidden caches. Strategic site during conflicts.
investigation_priorities.method: Metal detection + GPR + excavation of specific features (wells, cellars, foundation anomalies)
